name: Annamanada Mahadeva Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in Annamanada counted among the 108 ancient Shiva shrines of Kerala, unusual in that Parvati and Vishnu are installed alongside Shiva with equal standing. It is administered by the Cochin Devaswom Board and keeps Maha Shivaratri as its principal festival.
story: Tradition holds that the shrine was consecrated by the sage Parashurama, and its lingam is worshipped as Kirathamurthi granting the Pashupatastra to Arjuna.

name: Kalleshwara Temple, Hire Hadagali
significance: A twin-shrine soapstone temple raised about 1057 CE by Demarasa, a minister of the Western Chalukya king Someshvara I, and enlarged by later additions recorded in Old Kannada inscriptions. It is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India as a monument of national importance.

name: Anikkattilammakshethram
deity: Shiva and Parvati (Jagat Pita and Jagat Mata)
significance: A temple on the bank of the Manimala river where Shiva and Parvati are enshrined together in a single sanctum, a pairing said to be among the rarest in Kerala. Its eight-day Pongala in the month of Kumbham draws thousands of women who cook offerings along a two-kilometre stretch around the shrine.

name: Maruthamalai Marudhachalamurthy Temple
significance: A hill temple to Murugan set on a granite outcrop about 12 km west of Coimbatore in the Western Ghats, run by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE department. It is popularly counted as a seventh addition to the Six Abodes of Murugan.
story: The sage Pambatti Siddhar is said to have done penance here, to whom Murugan first appeared as a serpent and then in his own form with Valli and Devasena.

name: Karingattukavu Devi Temple
significance: A goddess temple on the bank of the Pampa at Prayar in Chengannur taluk, dedicated jointly to Durga and Bhadrakali. Its annual festival falls in the Malayalam month of Meenam, with Karthika as the chief day.

name: Kovur Sundareswarar Temple
significance: A south-facing Shiva temple with a seven-tiered rajagopuram on the western edge of Chennai, counted among the city's Navagraha temples. The Carnatic composer Tyagaraja composed the five songs of the Kovur Pancharatnam here.
story: The place is said to take its name from Mahalakshmi, who came to the spot in the form of a cow to worship Shiva.

name: Kanjiramvila Bhagavathi Temple
significance: A Bhagavathy temple at Chathannoor in Kollam district that serves as both a pilgrimage centre and a local tourist draw. Its Gajamela elephant pageant is the occasion that brings the largest crowds, including foreign visitors.

name: Kottekkad Temple
significance: A village temple about 8 km from Thrissur whose sanctum holds Bhagavathi. Several further consecrations stand in the compound, among them Shiva, Hanuman, Ayyappan, Subrahmanya, the serpent deities and Brahmarakshassu.

name: Karimpuzha Sree Ramaswamy Temple
significance: A Rama temple on the bank of the Karimpuzha river in Palakkad district, historically held by the Eralpad, heir to the Zamorin of Kozhikode. It is described as one of the rare Mahakshetrams of Kerala and is known locally as Dakshina Ayodhya.
story: Local tradition identifies the Karimpuzha with the Sarayu and holds that Rama ended his earthly life in its waters, which is why Hanuman, his companion in those last moments, is enshrined within the temple.

name: Krishnaswami Temple, Muthialpet
significance: A Krishna temple in the old George Town quarter of Chennai, completed in the 18th century. It became the flashpoint of the 1787 riot between the Left-hand and Right-hand caste groupings, which the Madras Presidency authorities had to mediate.

name: Budha Ganesha Temple
significance: An 11th-century khondalite shrine near the Dasashwamedh Ghat of the Baitarani, enshrining Ganesha in an aged form. Loose sculptures of Vishnu, Mahishamardini and the Jain Tirthankara Shantinath are kept at the site, and Ganesh Chaturthi is its main festival.

name: Annakoteshvara Temple
significance: A pancharatha Shiva temple of Suryavamsi Gajapati date at Latadeipur in Dhenkanal district, combining a rekha deula with a pidha hall. It is listed as a protected monument by the Archaeological Survey of India.
story: The temple's lingam is said to have been dislodged during the raids of Kalapahad, the general who invaded Odisha from Bengal.

name: Kopineshwar Mandir
significance: Thane's principal Shiva temple, founded under the Shilahara dynasty and rebuilt in 1760 with further renovations in 1879 and 1996. Its lingam, about 12 feet across, is among the largest in Maharashtra, and Shiva here is treated as the patron deity of the city.

name: Apparswami Temple
deity: Apparswami (Shaivite saint), worshipped as a shivalinga
significance: A Shaivite shrine on Royapettah High Road in Chennai raised over the tomb of Apparswami, a 19th-century saint. His chief disciple Chidambaraswamy set a shivalinga above the grave, around which the temple grew.

name: Budha Deula
deity: Shiva (twin lingams on a shared yonipitha)
significance: An east-facing Shiva shrine at Badu Sahi in the old town of Bhubaneswar, holding two lingams on a single circular yonipitha plus four more recovered from the Bindusagar tank. It stands between the Bindusagar, the Mohini temple and the Akhada Chandi temple, and is used for sradha and other funerary rites.

name: Kanila Shree Bhagavathi Temple
significance: A Bhagavati temple in Manjeshwaram taluk of Kasaragod district, standing beside the coastal highway about a kilometre north of Hosangadi junction. The trust also runs an arts and culture hall and an English-medium school on the temple grounds.

name: Tiger Cave
significance: A Pallava rock-cut shrine near Mahabalipuram, its portico framed by a crown of carved tiger heads, attributed to the reign of Rajasimha Narasimhavarman II. An inscription found in the complex in 2005 led to the excavation of an older Murugan temple of Sangam date nearby; the site is maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India.

name: Kasi Viswanatha Temple, Ayanavaram
significance: A Shiva temple on Konnur High Road in Ayanavaram, Chennai, built during East India Company rule by the Tawker family of the city's Gujarati merchant community. It is now administered by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE department.

name: Kozha Sree Narasimhaswami Temple
significance: A Narasimha temple at Kozha near Kuravilangad, reckoned among the older shrines of Kerala and lying in territory that belonged to the Vadakkumkoor principality until about 1752. Narasimha is worshipped here in his calm aspect after the killing of Hiranyakashipu, and Narasimha Jayanti is the chief festival.
story: The image is held to be swayambhu, found in the forest by a hunter, whom some traditions identify as Shiva himself, and consecrated by the local people.

name: Koteshwar Mahadev
significance: A cave shrine to Shiva on the Alaknanda about 3 km from Rudraprayag town, at roughly 885 m. Mahashivratri is its main observance, and a 60-bed charitable hospital run by a Shankaracharya trust adjoins the temple.
story: Shiva is said to have paused to meditate in this cave on his way to Kedarnath while eluding the demon Bhasmasura, whom he later destroyed.

name: Arattupuzha Temple
significance: A Dharma Sastha temple near Thrissur under the Cochin Devaswom Board, best known for the Arattupuzha Pooram, the oldest of Kerala's pooram festivals. The pooram is styled a Devamela, the yearly gathering of the region's deities.
story: The deity is believed to carry the vital force of Vasishta, family preceptor of the Raghu line and teacher of Rama, and the temple is said to be three thousand years old.

name: Kartikeya Temple, Pehowa
significance: A Nagara-style shrine at Pehowa in Kurukshetra district, described as one of the oldest Kartikeya temples in north India. It worships the god in his celibate form, and women are barred from entering.
story: The Skanda Purana account followed here has Kartikeya born of the fire of Shiva's third eye, carried by Agni and Ganga, reared by the six Pleiades in a reed thicket and grown to six faces before slaying the demon Taraka.

name: Chammanad Devi Temple
significance: A Bhadrakali temple at Kodamthuruth near Ezhupunna, midway between Vyttila and Cherthala, held and run by the eight households of the Ettu Veettil Kartha family. Its ten-day Utsavam falls in the Malayalam month of Kumbham, and two subsidiary shrines to Sastha and Krishna belong to it.

name: Brahmani Temple
significance: A laterite pidha-vimana temple of Somavamsi date at Avana in Balasore district, pancharatha in plan, enshrining a chlorite image of Chamunda. It remains in worship and is a protected monument of the Odisha State Archaeology, its loose sculpture including a four-armed Avalokiteshvara that points to a Buddhist presence at the site.

name: Ampal Brahmapureeswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple at Ambal in Tiruvarur district, held to be the last of the sixty raised-platform maadakoil shrines built by Kochengat Chola, with a three-tiered rajagopuram. It is one of the 275 Paadal Petra Sthalams, sung by Tirugnanasambandar in the Tevaram, and is run by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE department.
story: Brahma, cursed by Shiva, is said to have worshipped here and bathed in the temple tank Annam Poigai to regain his form.

name: Kote Jalakantheshwara Temple
significance: A Shiva temple of Chola date near Kalasipalya in old Bangalore, renovated by Kempegowda, the city's founder. It is unusual in carrying three sanctums, to Jalakantheshwara, Parvati and Kailashnathar.

name: Kottarakkulam Sree Mahaganapathy Kovil
significance: An old Ganesha shrine in Kollam town rebuilt into its present form in 1984, also housing Nagaraja and Ayyappan. It is maintained by the roughly 270 Tamil Brahmin families of Kollam and is known for its Ashta Dravya Mahaganapathy Homam and Vinayaka Chaturthi celebrations.

name: Kapilash Temple
significance: A hill temple to Shiva as Chandrasekhar in Dhenkanal district, dated by its inscriptions to 1246 and credited to the Eastern Ganga king Narasingha Deva I. Its 60-foot tower stands at about 2,239 feet, reached by a flight of 1,352 steps, and shrines to Ganesha, Kartikeya, Ganga, Jagannath and Vishwanath share the complex.
story: The hill is identified with the ashram of the sage Kapila and is called by some a second Kailash of Shiva.

name: Asramam Sree Krishna Swamy Temple
significance: A Krishna temple on the shore of Ashtamudi Lake at Asramam in Kollam, raised on a mound of earth dug from what is now its tank. Its ten-day festival ends in the Kollam Pooram in mid-April, and the compound holds a separate Ayyappan shrine with the eighteen steps of Sabarimala.

name: Kamakshi Amman Temple, Mangadu
significance: A temple in the Chennai suburb of Mangadu where Parvati is worshipped as Tapas Kamakshi, the goddess at her penance. Its chief object of worship is an Ardhameru yantra that receives only kumkum offerings, and the seven-tiered rajagopuram is a recent addition; the temple is run by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE department.
story: Parvati is said to have done severe penance on this spot, standing amid fire with one foot raised, to rejoin Shiva after playfully covering his eyes, and Adi Shankara is held to have installed the Ardhameru chakra to cool the heat of her austerity.

name: Chakkulathukavu Temple
significance: A Durga temple on the Pampa at Neerattupuram, about 9 km from Thiruvalla, which grew from a family shrine into one of Kerala's best-known temples. Its Pongala in the month of Vrischikam draws hundreds of thousands of women, and it also keeps the twelve-day Panthrandu Noyampu fast and the Naree Pooja.

name: Cherthala Karthyayani Devi Temple
significance: The principal temple of Cherthala, where the goddess is worshipped in an aniconic form set below ground level and held to be self-manifested. Its Cherthala Pooram is reckoned second among Kerala's poorams and is unusual for an Aarattu performed twice daily; Gandhi addressed a gathering here on 18 January 1937.
story: The saint Vilwamangalam Swamiyar is said to have consecrated the goddess at this spot on his way back from installing the deity at the Padmanabhaswamy temple in Thiruvananthapuram.

name: Budhanath Temple
significance: A Shaivite temple on the Ganga at Jogsar in Bhagalpur, counted among the 108 Nath shrines named in the Shiva Purana, with a lingam regarded as self-manifested. It draws more than a million pilgrims through the month of Shravan and is the starting point of an annual Kanwar Yatra to Basukinath.
story: Tradition places its origin in the Treta Yuga and credits its consecration to the sage Vashishtha, while the image of Bhavani in the compound is said to have floated down the Ganga from Munger.

name: Ram Mandir, Bhubaneswar
significance: A privately endowed temple near Kharavel Nagar on Janpath in Bhubaneswar, holding marble images of Rama, Sita and Lakshmana with further shrines to Hanuman and Shiva. Its tall spire is a landmark of the city, and it keeps Ram Navami, Vivaha Panchami and a Raksha Bandhan fair.

name: Kottukal Cave Temple
significance: A rock-cut shrine near Anchal in Kollam district, two chambers hewn under a single boulder with a monolithic Nandi, dated by historians to about the 7th century and credited to the ruler Nedila Paranthaka Nedumchadayan of Chadayamangalam. It is held to be contemporary with the Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram and is now served by the Travancore Devaswom Board.
story: Local tradition says the great rock was carried to the spot by Shiva in his several forms, Nandi among them.

name: Kripamayee Kali Temple
significance: A nine-spired nabaratna Kali temple on the east bank of the Hooghly at Baranagar, founded in 1848 by the zamindar and Kali devotee Jai Narayan Mitra on land he bought for the purpose. Twelve Shiva shrines stand within the compound, and the site is also known as Joy Mitra Kalibari.

name: Kasi Viswanatha Temple, West Mambalam
significance: A 17th-century Shiva temple in West Mambalam, Chennai, named for the Vishwanatha temple at Varanasi and also called Mahabilva Kshetra. It is run by the Tamil Nadu HR&CE department, which conducted its kumbhabhishekam in September 2023.

name: Koothanur Maha Saraswathi Temple
significance: The only temple in Tamil Nadu with Saraswati as its presiding deity, at Koothanur in Tiruvarur district; shrines to her are rare anywhere in India. The medieval Tamil poets Ottakoothar and Kambar sang of it, and Vijayadasami is its chief festival.

name: Ananthasayana Temple
significance: A temple near Hampi raised in 1524 by Krishnadevaraya in memory of his dead son, its long rectangular sanctuary entered through triple doorways under a vaulted roof some 24 metres high. It falls within the Group of Monuments at Hampi, inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 1986.
story: The image is said to have been carried here under an injunction not to look back; when the guide broke it, the figure would move no further and stayed at Holalu.

name: Anandavalleeshwaram Sri Mahadevar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in Kollam city completed in the 11th century, its teak sanctum housing Shiva facing west and Parvati as Anandavally facing east. It is counted among the 108 principal Shiva temples of Kerala, and its ten-day festival falls in the month of Meenam.
story: Folklore credits the installation of the lingam here to the sage Parashurama.

name: Brahmeshvara Temple, Kikkeri
significance: A Hoysala temple at Kikkeri finished in 1171, paid for by a woman named Bammave Nayakiti in the reign of Narasimha I, and drawing Shaiva, Vaishnava and Shakta imagery together. Its aedicules reproduce Nagara, Dravida, Vesara, Bhumija and hybrid tower forms, and it is a protected monument of the Karnataka heritage department.
story: Village tradition holds that a tribal chief named Keeka asked a king for a settlement bearing his name, complete with temple, tank and fort.

name: Karaikal Ammaiyar Temple
deity: Karaikal Ammaiyar (Punithavathi), with Somanathar and Somanayaki
significance: A temple on Bharathiar Street in Karaikal built in 1929 by Malaiperumal Pillai for Punithavathi, known as Karaikal Ammaiyar, the foremost woman among the sixty-three Nayanmars of Saiva Siddhanta.
story: She is remembered for feeding Shiva as the mendicant Bhikshatana with curd rice and mangoes, which is why mangoes are given out at the Mangani Tirunal on the full moon of Aani.
